summary: The flute was played at the Simchas Beis HaShoeivah, the great celebration of drawing water in the Beis HaMikdash. Anyone who never saw it never saw real simcha.

chunks.en: The flute: five or six days.
chunks.st: The flute is played on the festival of Sukkot for five or six days.

chunks.en: This is the flute of the Simchas Beis HaShoeivah,
chunks.explain: The celebration for drawing the water to pour on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: This is the flute of the Place of the Drawing of the Water,

chunks.en: which does not push aside Shabbos
chunks.explain: So it is not played on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whose playing overrides neither Shabbat

chunks.en: or Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor the Festival.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, if the first Festival day occurred on Shabbat, they would play the flute for six days that year. However, if Shabbat coincided with one of the intermediate days of the Festival, they would play the flute for only five days.

chunks.en: They said: anyone who did not see
chunks.st: One who did not see

chunks.en: the Simchas Beis HaShoeivah
chunks.st: the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing of the Water

chunks.en: never saw simcha in his life.
chunks.st: never saw celebration in his days.

summary: At the end of the first day of Sukkos, they made the Women's Courtyard ready for the big celebration. There were tall golden menoros with bowls on top, and young Kohanim climbed ladders to fill them with oil.
stIntro: This was the sequence of events:

chunks.he: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חָג,
chunks.en: At the end of the first Yom Tov of the chag,
chunks.st: At the conclusion of the first Festival day

chunks.en: they went down to the Women's Courtyard,
chunks.st: the priests and the Levites descended from the Israelites’ courtyard to the Women’s Courtyard,

chunks.en: and made a big fix there.
chunks.explain: They built a balcony so the men and the women would be apart.
chunks.st: where they would introduce a significant repair,

chunks.en: And there were golden menoros there,
chunks.st: There were golden candelabra atop poles there in the courtyard.

chunks.en: and four golden bowls on top of each one,
chunks.st: And there were four basins made of gold at the top of each candelabrum.

chunks.en: and four ladders for each and every one,
chunks.st: And there were four ladders for each and every pole

chunks.he: וְאַרְבָּעָה יְלָדִים מִפִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה וּבִידֵיהֶם כַּדִּים
chunks.en: and four young Kohanim, and in their hands were jugs
chunks.explain: Pirchei kehunah are young boys from Kohen families who are training to serve.
chunks.st: and there were four children from the priesthood trainees, and in their hands were pitchers

chunks.he: שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים לֹג,
chunks.en: of oil, holding one hundred and twenty lugin,
chunks.st: with a capacity of 120 log of oil

chunks.en: that they pour into each and every bowl.
chunks.st: that they would pour into each and every basin.

summary: The wicks for the menoros were made from the old clothes of the Kohanim. The light was so strong that every courtyard in Yerushalayim was lit up.

chunks.en: From the worn-out pants of the Kohanim and from their belts,
chunks.st: From the worn trousers of the priests and their belts

chunks.en: from them they would tear strips,
chunks.explain: They used the strips as wicks.
chunks.st: they would loosen and tear strips to use as wicks,

chunks.en: and with them they would light.
chunks.st: and with them they would light the candelabra.

chunks.en: And there was no courtyard in Yerushalayim that was not
chunks.st: And the light from the candelabra was so bright that there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem that was not

chunks.en: lit up by the light of the Beis HaShoeivah.
chunks.st: illuminated from the light of the Place of the Drawing of the Water.

summary: At the Simchas Beis HaShoeivah, great tzaddikim danced with torches, and the Levi'im played music on fifteen steps. At dawn the Kohanim blew trumpets and walked to the eastern gate, then turned to face the Beis HaMikdash and said, "Our eyes are to Hashem."

chunks.en: Pious people and men of good deeds would dance
chunks.st: The pious and the men of action would dance

chunks.en: in front of them, with burning torches in their hands,
chunks.st: before the people who attended the celebration, with flaming torches that they would juggle in their hands,

chunks.en: and they would say songs and praises before them.
chunks.st: and they would say before them passages of song and praise to God.

chunks.en: And the Levi'im played on harps, lyres, cymbals and trumpets,
chunks.st: And the Levites would play on lyres, harps, cymbals, and trumpets,

chunks.en: and on so many musical instruments that they could not be counted,
chunks.st: and countless other musical instruments.

chunks.en: on the fifteen steps that go down
chunks.st: The musicians would stand on the fifteen stairs that descend

chunks.en: from the Israelites' Courtyard to the Women's Courtyard,
chunks.st: from the Israelites’ courtyard to the Women’s Courtyard,

chunks.he: כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּהִלִּים,
chunks.en: like the fifteen Shir HaMa'alos in Tehillim,
chunks.explain: Fifteen chapters of Tehillim start with "Shir HaMa'alos."
chunks.st: corresponding to the fifteen Songs of the Ascents in Psalms,

chunks.en: on which the Levi'im stand with musical instruments
chunks.st: and upon which the Levites stand with musical instruments

chunks.en: and sing.
chunks.st: and recite their song.

chunks.en: And two Kohanim stood at the upper gate
chunks.st: And this was the ceremony of the Water Libation: Two priests stood at the Upper Gate

chunks.en: that goes down from the Israelites' Courtyard to the Women's Courtyard,
chunks.st: that descends from the Israelites’ courtyard to the Women’s Courtyard,

chunks.en: with two trumpets in their hands.
chunks.st: with two trumpets in their hands.

chunks.en: When the rooster crowed,
chunks.st: When the rooster crowed at dawn,

chunks.en: they blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.st: they sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.

chunks.en: When they reached the tenth step,
chunks.explain: The people going to draw the water.
chunks.st: When they who would draw the water reached the tenth stair

chunks.en: they blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.st: the trumpeters sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia,
chunks.stMore: to indicate that the time to draw water from the Siloam pool had arrived.

chunks.en: When they reached the courtyard,
chunks.st: When they reached the Women’s Courtyard with the basins of water in their hands,

chunks.en: they blew a tekiah, a teruah, and a tekiah.
chunks.st: the trumpeters sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.
chunks.stMore: When they reached the ground of the Women’s Courtyard, the trumpeters sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.

chunks.en: They kept blowing as they walked,
chunks.st: They continued sounding the trumpets

chunks.en: until they reached the gate that goes out to the east.
chunks.st: until they reached the gate through which one exits to the east,
chunks.stMore: from the Women’s Courtyard to the eastern slope of the Temple Mount.

chunks.en: When they reached the gate that goes out to the east,
chunks.st: When they reached the gate through which one exits to the east,

chunks.en: they turned their faces to the west,
chunks.explain: Toward the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: they turned from facing east to facing west, toward the Holy of Holies,

chunks.he: וְאָמְרוּ, אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ בַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם
chunks.en: and said, "Our fathers who were in this place stood with their backs
chunks.explain: Some people in the time of the first Beis HaMikdash did not act the right way.
chunks.st: and said: Our ancestors who were in this place during the First Temple period who did not conduct themselves appropriately, stood “with their backs

chunks.en: to the Heichal of Hashem and their faces to the east,
chunks.st: toward the Sanctuary of the Lord, and their faces toward the east;

words.note: The Heichal is the holy building of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and they bowed eastward to the sun,
chunks.explain: They served the sun as an idol.
chunks.st: and they worshipped the sun toward the east” (Ezekiel 8:16),

chunks.en: but as for us, our eyes are to Hashem."
chunks.st: and we, our eyes are to God.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says that

chunks.en: they would say it again:
chunks.st: they would repeat and say:

chunks.en: "We are Hashem's,
chunks.st: We are to God,

chunks.en: and our eyes are to Hashem."
chunks.st: and our eyes are to God.

summary: Every day in the Beis HaMikdash the trumpets were blown at least twenty-one times, and never more than forty-eight. This mishnah counts the blasts on a regular day, on Erev Shabbos, and on Erev Shabbos during Sukkos.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת תְּקִיעוֹת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: We do not blow fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: One sounds no fewer than twenty-one trumpet blasts in the Temple,

chunks.en: and we do not blow more than forty-eight.
chunks.st: and one sounds no more than forty-eight.

chunks.en: Every day there were
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: Each day there were

chunks.en: twenty-one blasts in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: twenty-one trumpet blasts in the Temple:

chunks.en: three for opening the gates,
chunks.st: Three blasts were sounded for the opening of the gates in the morning,

chunks.en: and nine for the morning korban tamid,
chunks.explain: The tamid is a korban brought every morning and every afternoon.
chunks.st: nine for the daily morning offering,

chunks.en: and nine for the afternoon korban tamid.
chunks.st: and nine for the daily afternoon offering, totaling twenty-one.

chunks.en: And for the korban mussaf they would add nine more.
chunks.explain: On days like Rosh Chodesh there is an extra korban, the mussaf.
chunks.st: And on a day when the additional offerings were sacrificed, e.g., the New Moon, with the additional offerings they would add nine additional blasts.

chunks.he: וּבְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיוּ מוֹסִיפִין עוֹד שֵׁשׁ,
chunks.en: And on Erev Shabbos they would add six more:
chunks.st: And on Shabbat eve they would add six blasts
chunks.stMore: sounded adjacent to the onset of Shabbat:

chunks.en: three to make the people stop working,
chunks.st: Three to stop the people from their labor,
chunks.stMore: as the blasts inform the people that Shabbat is approaching and they stop working,

chunks.en: and three to separate between holy and weekday.
chunks.explain: To show that Shabbos is starting.
chunks.st: and three at the onset of Shabbat to demarcate between sacred and profane.

chunks.en: On Erev Shabbos during the chag,
chunks.st: On Shabbat eve during the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: there were forty-eight:
chunks.st: there were forty-eight blasts. How so?

chunks.en: three for opening the gates,
chunks.st: Three in the morning for the opening of the gates;

chunks.en: three for the upper gate,
chunks.st: three for the upper gate;

chunks.en: and three for the lower gate,
chunks.st: and three for the lower gate;

chunks.en: and three for filling the water,
chunks.explain: The water that is poured on the mizbe'ach on Sukkos.
chunks.st: and three for the filling of the vessel with water,
chunks.stMore: as described in the sequence of the ritual of drawing the water for the water libation (48b);

chunks.en: and three on top of the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: and three when pouring the water libation upon the altar;

chunks.en: nine for the morning korban tamid,
chunks.st: nine for the daily morning offering;

chunks.en: and nine for the afternoon korban tamid,
chunks.st: and nine for the daily afternoon offering;

chunks.en: and nine for the korban mussaf,
chunks.st: and nine for the additional offerings;

chunks.he: שָׁלשׁ לְהַבְטִיל אֶת הָעָם מִן הַמְּלָאכָה,
chunks.en: three to make the people stop working,
chunks.st: three to stop the people from work;

chunks.en: and three to separate between holy and weekday.
chunks.st: and three more to demarcate between sacred and profane, totaling forty-eight blasts.

summary: On Sukkos many korbanos were brought, and all twenty-four groups of Kohanim shared them. This mishnah tells how the bulls, rams, goat and sheep were split among the groups each day, so that everyone got a turn.

chunks.en: On the first day of the chag
chunks.st: On the first Festival day of Sukkot

chunks.en: there were thirteen bulls,
chunks.st: there were thirteen bulls,

chunks.en: and two rams,
chunks.st: two rams,

chunks.en: and one goat.
chunks.explain: Each of these went to a different group of Kohanim.
chunks.st: and one goat there.
chunks.stMore: The mishna proceeds to discuss the division of labor for the Festival offerings among the twenty-four priestly watches, all of which serve in the Temple on the pilgrimage Festivals. The sixteen offerings mentioned above were divided among sixteen priestly watches, one offering per watch.

chunks.en: There were fourteen left
chunks.st: Fourteen

chunks.en: sheep for eight groups of Kohanim.
chunks.st: sheep remained to be divided among the eight remaining watches.

words.note: A mishmar is one of the 24 groups of Kohanim who took turns serving.

chunks.en: On the first day,
chunks.st: On the first day of the Festival,

chunks.en: six groups bring two each,
chunks.st: six of the eight remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each for a total of twelve,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining two watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the second day, five bring two each,
chunks.explain: There was one bull fewer each day.
chunks.st: On the second day of the Festival, i.e., the first day of the intermediate days, when twelve bulls were sacrificed, fifteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, five of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining four watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the third day, four bring two each,
chunks.st: On the third day of the Festival, when eleven bulls were sacrificed, fourteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, four of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining six watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the fourth day, three bring two each,
chunks.st: On the fourth day of the Festival, when ten bulls were sacrificed, thirteen of the priestly watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, three of the remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining eight watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the fifth day, two bring two each,
chunks.st: On the fifth day, when nine bulls were sacrificed, twelve watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, two of the twelve remaining watches sacrifice two sheep each,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining ten watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the sixth day, one brings two,
chunks.st: On the sixth day, when eight bulls were sacrificed, eleven watches sacrifice the bulls, rams, and goat, one of the remaining watches sacrifices two sheep,

chunks.en: and the rest bring one each.
chunks.st: and the remaining twelve watches sacrifice one sheep each.

chunks.en: On the seventh day, they are all equal.
chunks.st: On the seventh day they are all equal

chunks.en: On the eighth day, they went back to the lottery, like on the other Yamim Tovim.
chunks.explain: A lottery was a way of choosing who gets each job.
chunks.st: On the eighth day, when there was a completely different configuration of offerings, they returned to the standard lottery system used to determine which of the priestly watches would sacrifice the offerings, as they did on the other pilgrimage Festivals,
chunks.stMore: which do not have as many offerings as does Sukkot.

chunks.en: They said, a group that brought bulls today
chunks.st: They said about the ordering of the priestly watches: One who sacrificed bulls today

chunks.en: should not bring bulls tomorrow,
chunks.st: will not sacrifice bulls tomorrow;

chunks.en: but they take turns, round and round.
chunks.st: rather, they will sacrifice one of the other types of offerings. They rotate,
chunks.stMore: so that each of the watches will have the opportunity to sacrifice bulls as well as other animals.

summary: On the three Regalim, all twenty-four groups of Kohanim share the korbanos and the lechem hapanim. But the group whose week it is still brings the regular korbanos.

chunks.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה הָיוּ כָּל מִשְׁמָרוֹת
chunks.en: Three times a year all the groups of Kohanim were
chunks.st: At three times during the year, all twenty-four priestly watches

chunks.he: שָׁווֹת בְּאֵמוּרֵי הָרְגָלִים וּבְחִלּוּק לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
chunks.en: equal in the korbanos of the Yom Tov and in sharing the lechem hapanim.
chunks.explain: The lechem hapanim is the special bread on the Shulchan in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: have equal status, in that all receive a share in the Temple service independent of the standard order of the watches and all receive a share in the accompanying gifts of the priesthood: In the portions of the offerings of the Festivals sacrificed on the altar and in the distribution of the shewbread on Shabbat during the Festivals.

chunks.en: On Shavuos they say to each Kohen,
chunks.st: On Shavuot that coincides with Shabbat, when the two loaves offered on Shavuot would be distributed together with the distribution of the shewbread, the priest charged with the distribution says to each priest:

chunks.en: "Here is matzah, here is chametz."
chunks.explain: The lechem hapanim was matzah, and the special Shavuos bread was chametz.
chunks.st: Here is matza from the shewbread for you, and here is leavened bread from the two loaves for you.

chunks.en: The group whose time is set,
chunks.st: The principle is that the priestly watch whose time is fixed during the Festival

chunks.en: brings the korban tamid,
chunks.st: sacrifices the daily offerings

chunks.en: korbanos people promised or gave, and the other korbanos of the public,
chunks.st: during the Festival, as well as vow-offerings, free-will offerings, and all other communal offerings.

chunks.en: and it brings all of them.
chunks.st: And that watch sacrifices all of them
chunks.stMore: even during the Festival, when other aspects of the service are shared by all the watches.

chunks.en: A Yom Tov that is right next to Shabbos,
chunks.st: In the case of a Festival that occurs adjacent to Shabbat,

chunks.en: whether before it or after it,
chunks.st: both when it occurs preceding it and when it occurs following it,

chunks.en: all the groups were equal
chunks.st: all the watches that arrived early or remained late to serve in the Temple were of equal status

chunks.en: in sharing the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: in the distribution of the shewbread on that Shabbat.

summary: This mishnah tells how the lechem hapanim was split between groups of Kohanim. The group of Bilga was given a punishment: it always shared in the south, its ring was fixed and its cubby was closed.

chunks.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אֶחָד לְהַפְסִיק בֵּינְתַיִם,
chunks.en: If there happened to be one day in between,
chunks.explain: One day between Yom Tov and Shabbos.
chunks.st: If one day happened to separate between the Festival and Shabbat,

chunks.en: the group whose time is set,
chunks.st: the watch whose time was scheduled

chunks.en: would take ten loaves,
chunks.st: would take ten of the twelve loaves of shewbread,

chunks.en: and the group that stayed later takes two.
chunks.explain: They stayed because there was no time to get home before Shabbos.
chunks.st: and the watch that was detained after the Festival because there was insufficient time to get home before Shabbat takes two loaves.

chunks.en: And on the rest of the days of the year,
chunks.st: And during the rest of the days of the year,
chunks.stMore: when the changing of the watches takes place on Shabbat,

chunks.en: the group coming in takes six,
chunks.st: the incoming watch takes six loaves

chunks.en: and the group going out takes six.
chunks.st: and the outgoing watch takes six loaves.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the group coming in takes seven,
chunks.st: The incoming watch takes seven loaves

chunks.en: and the group going out takes five.
chunks.st: and the outgoing takes five.

chunks.en: The ones coming in share them in the north,
chunks.st: The standard procedure was that the members of the incoming watch divide the shewbread in the north section of the courtyard,

chunks.en: and the ones going out in the south.
chunks.st: and the outgoing watch in the south.

chunks.en: The group of Bilga always shares in the south,
chunks.explain: This was a punishment for the group of Bilga.
chunks.st: However, there was one exception: The watch of Bilga, due to a penalty imposed upon it, always divides the shewbread to its members in the south,

chunks.en: and its ring is fixed in place,
chunks.explain: They could not use their ring when preparing korbanos.
chunks.st: even when it is the incoming watch. And its ring used to facilitate slaughter of the animals was fixed in place,

chunks.en: and its cubby is closed up.
chunks.explain: Each group kept its knives and tools in a cubby in the wall.
chunks.st: and its niche among the niches in the wall of the Chamber of Knives, where the priests would store their knives and other vessels, was sealed.
